metadata.note: 1968 US Volkswagen Beetle 1500 (Type 1 / 113, 1,493 cc, 44 PS DIN): an air-cooled flat four, one exhaust valve a cylinder, firing 1-4-3-2 at even intervals. Valve: 32 mm (the stage auditor's reading); open 228.5 / 720 = 0.3174, from 44.5 BBDC / 4 ATDC at 1 mm lift, so shorter than the seat-to-seat openings the other sounds take; the nominal opening was not found. The stock Ernst silencer without an expansion chamber (K, 2026-11-24): each cylinder's primary runs from its port into the silencer and on within it to the nearer tail, the run within the silencer counted in its length, the four of one length (K); cylinders 1 and 4 join at the right (junction 0), 3 and 2 at the left (junction 1), and each side's tail runs to the open. Lengths from frames of a video of a stock Ernst silencer cut open (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OQlmITr10R8), scaled by the parts sellers' 614 mm between the connecting pipes and 335 mm between the outlets (+-4 %), the stage auditor's measurement: cylinders 2 and 4 (at the rear) run through the pipes crossing the silencer to the other side and leave them into the chamber through rows of holes, about 630 and 590 mm from the port; cylinders 1 and 3 (at the front) enter from below through the heat exchangers' tubes and end at the end chamber's dome, about 600 mm (not measured: an estimate from the design's equal lengths, +-50 mm). With the run within the chamber to the nearer tail (100 to 160 mm) the four come to 730 to 750 mm, written 0.74 m. The video's silencer is the type with two preheat pipes (1971 on), the 1968 car's the type with one; their connecting pipes are the same 614 mm apart, so the inside is taken as the same. Tails: the 1968 to 1974 part, 225 mm long, written 0.22 m. The tails' inner tubes and wool and the chambers' volumes are not written. Diameters: the real inner diameters, 32 mm (primaries) and 21 mm (tails), times 1.14 (36.5 and 24 mm). Lengths are in steps of 0.02 m.
